data.title: FTSE 100 extends gains – Christmas rally moves into focus
data.description:
The FTSE 100 is currently trading at 10,693 points. UK investors continue to favour commodity stocks heading into the weekend, with the sector benefiting from higher energy and precious metal prices. The upward momentum is being reinforced by some short covering in technology stocks.

In the UK, too, investors are increasingly focusing on the prospects of a Christmas rally. The backdrop for FTSE 100 companies has improved considerably over recent trading weeks, with fears of interest rate hikes now largely priced into the market. Investors are increasingly looking ahead to 2027 and the potential for easing inflationary pressures. It seems that, after all, the outlook may not be quite as daunting as investors initially feared.

data.title: DAX extends recovery – Black Friday puts market sentiment to the test
data.description:
The DAX is expected to extend its gains at the opening bell, with the index currently seen at around 25,350 points. Positive trading cues from Asia are providing further tailwinds. Chinese equity markets in particular are benefiting from news of measures to stabilise the domestic financial market. Meanwhile, inflation data from Japan came in slightly better than feared, with consumer prices in the Greater Tokyo area rising by 2.9%, just below expectations of 3%. The strong finish to the trading week across Asian markets is helping to put the turbulence seen earlier this week into perspective.

In Germany, investors are trying to make sense of SAP's announced job cuts. The software giant plans to eliminate 10,000 positions. The crucial question for investors is whether the company can improve efficiency through the adoption of new technologies or whether its underlying business is losing momentum. From an equity market perspective, job cuts driven by technological progress are a very different proposition from a cost-cutting programme born out of economic necessity.

Today's shortened trading session on Wall Street could prove particularly interesting. Black Friday is not only one of the most important shopping days of the year but, against the backdrop of renewed inflationary pressures, also a barometer of US consumer spending appetite. Holiday season sales are likely to provide important clues as to how resilient US private consumption really is.

Positive US equity futures are initially providing solid support for the DAX. Alongside several economic data releases still to come, the key question will be whether Wall Street investors carry the broadly positive sentiment across international equity markets into the weekend.

The German equity market has held up remarkably well during what has been a turbulent trading week. The recovery above the 25,000-point mark and subsequent gains suggest that investors' appetite for equities is returning. A positive finish to the week could see the DAX enter December with renewed momentum. The prospects of a Christmas rally have certainly improved. From a technical perspective, the DAX could trade within a range of 25,100 to 25,550 points today.

data.title: FTSE 100 extends gains – bargain hunters target beaten-down sectors
data.description:
The FTSE 100 is currently trading at 10,595 points, extending its gains from the previous session. The UK equity market is maintaining a positive tone, although trading remains confined to a relatively narrow range. The absence of trading cues from the United States is already noticeable this morning.

Technology and defence stocks are attracting particular buying interest on Thursday. Following a major contract win for Babcock, investors are taking a closer look at the European defence sector again. Tariff concerns are fading somewhat into the background, with gains in technology and commodity stocks helping to offset the associated uncertainty. Interest rate fears are also taking a back seat, at least for today. It remains to be seen how significantly higher energy prices will affect the economy and inflation in 2027. For now, investors are back on the hunt for bargains, selectively increasing their exposure to stocks in recently battered sectors with an eye on the coming trading year.

data.title: Brent oil may be gearing up for its next bull run
data.description:
Brent oil has fallen by as much as 25% since peaking on October 6, but it now appears to be gearing up for a bullish run. The technical chart is forming what looks like a falling wedge pattern, a bullish reversal pattern. This has been forming since 6 November, and a breakout from this pattern suggests Brent could head sharply higher.

Right now, Brent is also finding support around the $90 level, suggesting it could be gearing up for a big bounce if that support holds. A breakout above the $93 level would be needed to break out of the falling wedge pattern. That could send Brent surging, perhaps back toward $106, or even the highs set at the end of October near $118, based on that pattern.

Brent crude oil daily chart

Source: TradingView, 25 November 2026

Additionally, the chart shows further resistance at the 10-day exponential moving average, and horizontal resistance around $95 is Brent's biggest challenge. Once those three technical resistance levels encompass a range of $93 to $95, there is a fairly clean opportunity to run back toward $106.

Additionally, Brent's RSI has stopped falling and has been consolidating sideways while the price has continued to decline. This is a potential bullish divergence pattern, also suggesting that momentum in Brent may be shifting, and is something to watch. A breakout in the RSI above 42 could lead to a more bullish momentum swing.

The technical charts suggest Brent's sharp pullback may be nearing an end, and the pendulum is about to swing higher again.

data.title: FTSE 100 holds steady – investors remain on the sidelines ahead of US data deluge
data.description:
The FTSE 100 is currently trading unchanged at 10,510 points. UK investors are maintaining their cautious stance on Wednesday as they await the upcoming wave of macroeconomic data. For the time being, there is little reason to make any hasty investment decisions in the FTSE 100.

Index heavyweights BP and Shell continue to benefit from elevated energy prices, while other commodity stocks are tracking developments in precious and base metal prices. Recent retail sales and house price figures have been broadly stable and were met with little reaction from investors. With few domestic catalysts for UK equities today, investors are largely staying on the sidelines, watching developments in the technology sector from a distance. Given its relatively limited exposure to technology stocks, the FTSE 100 remains largely insulated from the turbulence currently affecting the global technology sector.

data.title: DAX defies market turmoil – fresh tariff threats and US data deluge in focus
data.description:
The DAX is expected to open at around 25,050 points. Despite renewed turbulence across international financial markets and weak trading cues from the United States and Asia, the index continues to hold above the psychologically important 25,000-point mark. AI stocks remain at the centre of the storm. At the same time, a familiar source of uncertainty is returning to financial markets in the form of renewed trade disputes.

The United States is aggressively pushing trade policy back onto the international agenda. A fresh round of punitive tariffs targeting 16 countries is looming and could particularly affect Germany's export-oriented companies. These are currently benefiting from the weakness of the euro against the US dollar. However, new trade barriers could quickly erode this competitive advantage.

Some encouragement is coming from better-than-expected quarterly results from US technology companies Dell and HP. Nevertheless, investors' attention is likely to shift increasingly from the technology sector towards the broader macroeconomic environment today. Just ahead of tomorrow's Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, financial markets are facing another substantial wave of economic data.

Following yesterday's significantly better-than-expected US consumer confidence figures, today's focus will be on durable goods orders, consumer spending, official US labour market data and gross domestic product. Particular attention is also likely to be paid to the PCE deflator, the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, as well as the central bank's Beige Book.

Investors are facing a dilemma: while a resilient US economy is generally good news for equity markets, it could further fuel fears of interest rate hikes if inflation remains persistently high. German GDP figures, meanwhile, failed to impress, falling short of expectations by 0.1 percentage points on both a quarterly and an annual basis. Elevated energy prices are likely to have weighed on both economic activity and private consumption. Supply chain disruptions and base effects resulting from declining order backlogs in the defence sector are also likely to have adversely affected production. The DAX could trade within a range of 24,950 to 25,250 points today.

data.title: FTSE 100 lacks momentum – investors await fresh impetus from Wall Street
data.description:
The FTSE 100 is currently trading at 10,480 points. Renewed weakness in commodity prices is weighing on shares in mining and energy companies, dampening investors' appetite for equities. Both energy commodities and precious metals are surrendering some of their recent gains today.

Wall Street holds the key

For UK investors, Tuesday is therefore shaping up to be a day of sitting back and waiting for developments. Fresh trading impetus could come from the upcoming US economic data and the subsequent trading session on Wall Street. The big question for now remains whether yesterday's gains were merely a flash in the pan or marked the beginning of a potential Santa Claus rally. The next few hours of trading in the United States should provide some answers.

data.title: DAX gains momentum – Huang rally faces its first real test
data.description:
The DAX is expected to open at around 25,400 points on Tuesday, extending its recent recovery. The dominant theme in equity markets remains Jensen Huang's surprise return to the helm of Nvidia. However, Asian equity markets have reacted very differently to his decision to reverse his resignation. While semiconductor-heavy markets in Japan and South Korea staged a spectacular rally, the response from Chinese equities was considerably more subdued.

Huang rally faces a test

Today brings the real test. It remains to be seen whether Huang's return has merely sparked a short-lived rally or can genuinely trigger a lasting shift in sentiment across the technology sector. The uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership has been resolved for now, but fundamental questions about the profitability of multibillion-dollar AI investments and elevated valuations remain. Nevertheless, the bulls have managed to get a foot back in the door.

Events at the start of the shortened US trading week have caught many market participants completely off guard. Few had anticipated such strong momentum. This is highly unusual for Black Friday week, when investors traditionally tend to adopt a more cautious stance. The flurry of economic data due over the next 48 hours could now determine whether this renewed confidence lasts through to the weekend.

Economic data moves into focus

In Germany, today's initial focus will be on the ifo Business Climate Index. Following Monday's better-than-expected purchasing managers' indices, a further improvement in business sentiment would send an encouraging signal for the German economy. In the afternoon, attention will turn to US labour market data and consumer confidence figures. Following yesterday's rather disappointing purchasing managers' indices, the key question will be whether weaker economic momentum is also reflected in household sentiment.

Huang's return has given equity markets a much-needed breathing space. Whether this marks the restart of the year-end rally, however, is likely to be determined less in Nvidia's boardroom than by the upcoming economic data. The DAX could trade within a range of 25,250 to 25,500 points today.

data.title: Tech stocks surge on Huang's return – DAX finds fresh hope
data.description:
The surprise return of Jensen Huang to the helm of Nvidia has sparked a powerful rally in technology stocks, giving the DAX fresh momentum and pushing it comfortably back above the 25,000-point mark. The semiconductor giant's board has reinstated its former chief executive as CEO and brought him back onto the board. The company is responding to mounting pressure from employees, investors and politicians. Even Elon Musk weighed in over the weekend, speculating on his platform X about a possible acquisition of a 50% stake in the company and the reinstatement of Nvidia's founder. The story had taken an increasingly bizarre turn. With Huang's return, some calm should now be restored, at least at the leadership level.

Regulatory and political challenges remain

However, the returning CEO faces a formidable list of challenges. The announced review of the company's accounts by the US Securities and Exchange Commission, allegations of espionage and political investigations into its links with China remain significant sources of uncertainty. Huang must now not only regain investors' trust but also resolve numerous regulatory and political problems. The visionary is back, but his toughest challenges may still lie ahead.

Technology shares could regain momentum

Nevertheless, the news could hardly have come at a better time for international equity markets. Following the sharp losses of recent trading sessions, Huang's return could trigger an important shift in sentiment across the technology sector. Semiconductor stocks, which have recently come under particularly heavy pressure, could benefit from renewed confidence. In recent weeks, investors have become increasingly critical of elevated AI valuations and multibillion-dollar investment programmes. There is now at least a chance that attention will shift back towards the industry's long-term growth prospects.

Investors in the DAX, meanwhile, face a dilemma. On the one hand, numerous German blue-chip stocks appear attractively valued again following the recent correction. On the other, turmoil in the US technology sector and renewed interest rate fears have significantly dampened buying appetite. However, encouraging purchasing managers' indices from Germany and other major economies suggest that the economic outlook is improving, at least to some extent.

DAX looks for lasting support above 25,000

For the DAX, the 25,000-point mark remains the crucial short-term reference level. Jensen Huang's return could provide precisely the positive catalyst that equity markets have been lacking recently. After all, the structural growth prospects of the AI industry remain intact, even if valuations at many companies have had to undergo a correction. The bulls therefore have fresh grounds for optimism. The problems facing the technology sector have certainly not disappeared overnight, but sentiment could improve more quickly than seemed possible following the recent market losses. If the recovery in US technology stocks proves sustainable, the DAX could also reclaim the 25,000-point mark on a lasting basis. The year-end rally may not be over after all.

data.title: The EUR/USD tests critical support ahead of US inflation data
data.description:
The EUR/USD is testing a minor support level ahead of a holiday-shortened trading week for US markets, with the important US PCE report due on the morning of 25 November. Analysts estimate that both headline and core PCE will rise by 0.3% on a month-over-month basis. Currently, markets are pricing in as many as two rate hikes from the Fed by the March meeting.

PCE could test support at $1.09

A stronger-than-expected PCE reading could push EUR/USD below support at $1.09 and potentially down to around $1.075. That would be the next major level of support for the FX rate. Additionally, the extension of the bear flag formed between September and early November suggests EUR/USD could decline to around $1.07 as well.

EUR/USD, July 2024 – present

Source: TradingView, 23 November 2026

Bearish momentum meets oversold conditions

Additionally, EUR/USD continues to exhibit very bearish momentum, with the relative strength index (RSI) trending lower since peaking in August. However, the RSI is currently below 30, suggesting that the currency pair may be approaching a period of consolidation. EUR/USD is also continuing to find some support around its lower Bollinger Band. This suggests that the currency pair could continue to drift lower as long as it remains within the lower Bollinger Band. However, should EUR/USD fall below the lower band, with the RSI also remaining below 30, it would suggest that the currency pair has become increasingly oversold.

EUR/USD, March 2026 – present
